property: Third-party modem vendors implement a compatible AT-prefixed command/result-code interface so existing communications software can control multiple modem brands through similar serial command strings.

date_or_range.notes: Hayes compatibility becomes an ecosystem property rather than an exact single-vendor implementation.

sources.locator: Hayes Technical Reference for Modem Users, command-set terminology and command/register descriptions
sources.supports: source command-family semantics and Hayes Standard AT Command Set identity
sources.notes: Later Hayes reference; earliest Smartmodem grammar still requires first-generation manuals.

sources.locator: IBM PS/2 OEM hardware guide, modem product descriptions
sources.supports: third-party products explicitly sold/described as Hayes or Smartmodem compatible
real software depending on AT initialization/dialing, CONNECT responses and escape/reset behavior
sources.notes: Shows why compatibility mattered to software portability.

negative_claims: This edge does not claim that all Hayes-compatible modems implement identical commands, registers, defaults or result codes.
This edge does not claim that Hayes compatibility was initially a formal standards-body standard.
This edge does not establish direct ancestry from Hayes commands to later cellular/3GPP AT command standards; that branch still needs documentary proof.
open_questions: Build a vendor/model compatibility matrix for Hayes, USRobotics, Telebit, Supra, MultiTech, Zoom and ZyXEL command sets.
Recover early communications-software modem-driver files and UUCP dialer definitions demonstrating compatibility assumptions.
Trace formal ETSI/3GPP AT-command specifications and determine what sources explicitly cite Hayes-style ancestry.
Separate core AT grammar inheritance from vendor-specific %, &, backslash, plus and other extension namespaces.
notes: Canonical de-facto-standard edge: software dependency and competitive implementation turn a product interface into an ecosystem convention without requiring exact identity.
